text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure is considered high (hypertension) when it reaches or exceeds 130/80 mm Hg, according to the guidelines from the American Heart Association.
Readings are measured using two numbers: systolic (top number, the pressure when your heart beats) and diastolic (bottom number, the pressure when your heart rests between beats).

list.snippet: Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg (systolic) and less than 80 mm Hg (diastolic)
Stage 1 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): 130–139 mm Hg (systolic) OR 80–89 mm Hg (diastolic)
Stage 2 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): 140 mm Hg or higher (systolic) OR 90 mm Hg or higher (diastolic)
Hypertensive Crisis / Severe Hypertension: Higher than 180 mm Hg (systolic) AND/OR higher than 120 mm Hg (diastolic)

text_blocks.snippet: What to Do for High Readings

list.snippet: Stage 1 or Stage 2: Schedule a visit with your health care provider to discuss lifestyle changes and potential medication.

Hypertensive Crisis (>180/120 mm Hg): Wait 5 minutes and retest. If your reading remains this high and you experience symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, backache, numbness, or vision changes, call 911 immediately.
